title: Kenyan Bhajia
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN115 is a Street Food category entry for Bhajia. The primary recipe with full heritage, cultural notes, and detailed technique is KEN018 (Authentic Kenyan Bhajia). Both describe the same dish — this entry serves users browsing the Street Food category.

desc: Kenyan Bhajia — wafer-thin potato slices in a spiced gram flour batter, fried until irresistibly crispy. One of Kenya's most popular street snacks. See KEN018 for the full recipe with complete heritage and cultural detail.
longDesc: Bhajia is the Kenyan street snack that stops you in your tracks — the smell of spiced gram flour batter frying, the sight of golden crispy slices piled up at the stall. The secret is the thin slice and the right batter thickness. Found everywhere from Mombasa Old Town to Nairobi food courts.
ingredients: 4 large potatoes — peeled and very thinly sliced (2—3mm)
¼ cup fresh coriander — finely chopped
steps: Slice potatoes 2—3mm thin. Pat completely dry.
Combine all batter ingredients except water. Mix well.
Gradually whisk in water to a medium-thick batter. Rest 5 minutes.
Dip potato slices in batter, let excess drip, and fry in batches for 3—4 minutes until golden.
Drain on a rack. Serve with tamarind chutney or pili pili.
chefTips: Rice flour in the batter is the secret to crispiness.
commonMistakes: Thick slices — do not cook through.
Wet potato — batter does not adhere.
